revisions.feedbackText: terminal signature approved, I'll do the ceremony at run end

changed.summary: The TERMINAL HUMAN SIGNATURE is RULED (was FILED-recommended since V100, amended V101): at run end the principal performs the signing ceremony — recomputing the terminal head from the chain bytes under the pinned verifier on his own environment, then signing the canonical terminal-review body. The P7→P9 suffix gains its closing human waypoint; the 'machine testimony with NO closing waypoint' sentence retires at the next build.

The (iv-c) binding-to-key map widening — the two decision clock fields (boot_epoch, monotonic_reading) added at V93 so the decide-within-D law has per-decision evidence without touching the ruled access-log schema — is CONFIRMED by the principal exactly as filed. The reversible flag becomes a confirmed part of the map's closed schema; the FILED-awaiting-confirmation language retires at the next build.

The replay-exhaustion rule is RULED: when interruptions consume all R_max renders of one object before the checker labels it, that object receives an ABSTAIN label and the run CONTINUES — the hard pre-BS-8f halt is superseded for this case. ABSTAIN joins the sealed hand-check label vocabulary; sample completeness becomes every-object-labeled with ABSTAIN a label; the chain pattern (exactly R_max render commits per object, no per-object label event) is unchanged. Fourth and final parked decision — the board is clear.

The referee-loop STOPPING RULE is ruled: kimi's cap. At most THREE more referee rounds (V114-V116) under the scope freeze; if CLEAR x2 arrives earlier the loop ends better than planned; otherwise the text loop ENDS at the cap and whatever findings remain become an enumerated, generated KNOWN-DEBT APPENDIX signed with the freeze. The build items (six tools, calibration HELD, slots, BS-1) still gate the freeze - the cap ends text refereeing, not the build. Fifth ruling of the evening.
